Simple game with a short story that was able to be a good game. It's a game where you make your own decisions, so each character is going through their own situations, and you must choose what you will answer on these situations. There's kind of a story on this game about the main character, which is the killer, that decided to kill his sister, because of his problematic childhood and stuff.

I liked this game, it's kind of repetitive, but it's not bad: The characters are well written; there's a good story behind them in each dialogue; the gameplay is simple and it's really fun exploring the house, even though it takes around 10 minutes to beat the game.

Besides the fact this game has no one playing it. My friend and I bought the game. We had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. The bots do try to murder you if they are the killer. They do collect resources and hoard them sometimes. This game is fun to play with friends. A dead game is only dead until people revive it. Does it need some optimization? Yeah, a bit, there is a delay in when the game announces someone dies. A mic bug that's solved by leaving the lobby and coming back. Those are my biggest issues. However, I love the look of it cause it's like those old PS2 games honestly. I've seen worse graphics. This game is fun and we bought it on a sale. Major props to the Dev who kept putting out content and bug fixes when the game slowed down. Even put out a Halloween event. I hope it comes out this year too, cause I would like to play it with my friends.

Huge W to the Thompson brothers! 

After hearing all praise surrounding their newest title, "Well Dweller", I decided to take a look into their catologue of games and play through all of them from oldest to newest. Sheepo was the first game of theirs I had completed and really gave me a tatse for the quality of the games they create. As of writing this review I have just 100% completed "Islets", and can't wait to continue with "Crypt Custodian!" Obviously this game does have sertain flaws to it especially when comparing it to Kyle and Eric's newer titles, but for their first game I was left very impressed with the creativity behind this title. Fun and sometimes challenging platforming, really viby music to accompany this game's soundtrack, and a super cute and gorgeous artstyle are all factors that have made me come to love Sheepo as a game. For sure would reccomend! ;)

A fast, chaotic, and pure adrenaline fueled action game, with a fun cartoon style presentation and an intense soundtrack that strongly pushes the pace, somewhat reminiscent of Hotline Miami.

It follows an old-school arcade structure with a three-star scoring system in each level. The idea works well, even if the base difficulty can quickly become frustrating. Fortunately, several options allow you to adjust the challenge to suit your preference.
Levels are short and well designed overall, featuring a varied set of enemies and a few boss fights. The shoe system adds gameplay variations, mostly for fun, though a few do meaningfully change how you approach combat.

Despite its strengths, the game becomes quite repetitive over time. Even though it does what it aims to do well, it’s simply not really my type of game. I had a good time, but no real want to go for full completion.

An incredibly beautiful game and a case study in good pacing. The puzzles are just easy enough that they don't wear out their welcome, and there is just enough traversal between each one to give you a break from the puzzle gameplay and an opportunity to enjoy the painting-like scenery. The many similarities to Miyazaki Hayao franchises were almost impossible for me to ignore, but they are done well enough that they feel more like a tribute than imitation. A very solid 8.5/10.
